book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: One male dog, note, could be malign

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the standard abbreviation for male
a pug is a small snub-nosed breed of dog
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a lone male dog might be a nasty, ill-natured creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malign' looks like an adjective about the dog, but here it is the verb: to speak ill of.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn someone is to call their honesty into question, a near synonym of the verb malign.

clue.text: One's home, taking in little good to eat

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral, is one; the 's makes the home belong to it

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: a nest is a home
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone's home has very little that is good to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body, to swallow or eat it.

clue.text: Stop finger becoming malformed with absence of female hormone

indicators.note: something becoming malformed is losing its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged
with the absence of something means without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A medical note: a finger becomes deformed because a female hormone is missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Progestin is a synthetic progestogen, acting like progesterone, a sex hormone of the female reproductive cycle.

clue.text: Offered to include excessive type of dance

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: gave means offered
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: Someone proposed an over-the-top kind of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is common British shorthand for 'over the top', meaning excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is a French dance of moderate tempo from the seventeenth century, so a type of dance.

clue.text: Equivalent to a store's foremost stock? One should dive in

indicators.note: diving in means plunging inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the foremost part of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of store
a shop's stock is its goods
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A question about what matches a shop's best stock, with someone urged to plunge in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One should dive in' reads like a closing invitation, but it tells the article for one to go inside the stock word, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is as good as another means it is practically the same, equivalent in effect.

clue.text: Task-master restored water supply around lake

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word is put round a single letter

parts.note: something restored has been rescued, saved
L is the abbreviation for lake
a river supplies water

explanation.surface: A boss who has got the water supply working again around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restored' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply means SAVED, which wraps round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A slave-driver is a harsh boss who works people relentlessly, a demanding taskmaster.

clue.text: How mail's disrupted, ignoring one current guideline?

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are put in a new order
ignoring something means leaving it out, so one letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A complaint about how the post is disrupted, with no guidance in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' does double work: it supplies the letter removed and hints at the electrical subject, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohm's law, that current equals voltage over resistance, is the basic rule that guides electrical calculations.

clue.text: Promotional item picked up stomach fact

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an ad is a promotional item
tum is an informal word for stomach

explanation.surface: A free gift turns out to carry a nutritional fact about the stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' often signals a homophone; here, in a down entry, it lifts AD upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a known fact used as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Left after broadcast about currently unknown bird

indicators.note: after places the letter for left at the end, behind the rest
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the pieces that follow

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it, scattering it widely
now means currently
Y is a mathematical unknown
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A bird has been left after something was broadcast about it, and nobody knows where it is now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' wants to be an anagram signal, but it is SOW in its farming sense, scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The snowy owl is a large white owl of the Arctic, a bird.

clue.text: Up with fashion but also in a rut

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fashionable, trendy, in the slang of the sixties
second meaning: literally having grooves, set in a groove or furrow

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses pull opposite ways: trendy and stuck in a rut; the older literal sense of the word is simply 'grooved'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means fashionable in slang, and literally means furnished with or lying in a groove, a rut.

clue.text: Tropical plant friend encountered as well? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means not the whole thing, so the last word loses its final letter

parts.note: a pal is a friend
past tense of meet
too means as well, also

explanation.surface: A note about a tropical plant and a friend met there as well, with a hedged afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: The palmetto is a small fan palm of the tropics and the American South, a tropical plant.

clue.text: Rioting etc in various places providing astonishing sight

indicators.note: rioting is wild disorder, so the letters that follow are thrown out of order
various suggests things spread in differing ways, so the letters are mixed about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Riots breaking out all over the place make a dramatic sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ETC and PLACES are mixed together; 'in' just joins the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is a striking or remarkable thing to see, a sight that makes people stare.

clue.text: One showing miserly behaviour — see preacher getting upset

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person upsets the preacher they go to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseparer is a stingy person, one who would shave the rind off cheese to save a crumb: a miser.

clue.text: Depression not starting with year exhibiting some irregularity

indicators.note: a word that is not starting has had its opening letter taken away

parts.note: a slump is an economic depression
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: An economic depression that has not got going yet, with some irregularity in the year's figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lumpy is uneven, full of bumps, so it exhibits some irregularity of surface or texture.

clue.text: I'd worry badly about wife after subject matter in stage show

indicators.note: after places the mixed letters behind the piece named next

parts.note: the theme is the subject matter of a work

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the mixed letters go round the next piece
done badly means done wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Someone frets about their wife and the content of a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The I'D WORRY letters wrap round W and are rearranged into MERRY WIDOW, which follows THEME, the subject matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merry Widow is Franz Lehar's 1905 operetta, a much-revived piece of musical theatre, so a stage show.

clue.text: Part 1, in fact, is rather sonorous

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pieces go within the next word

parts.note: 'in fact' is 'in deed', indeed: a deed is a fact, a thing done
PT is the abbreviation for part
the numeral written out as a word

explanation.surface: Part one of a work is, in truth, somewhat resonant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' reads as a phrase meaning 'actually', but 'in' is the container signal and 'fact' alone is DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-toned voice or instrument has a low, resonant sound, which is what sonorous means.

clue.text: Wild cunning deployed in terror, bumping off leader

indicators.note: something deployed in a place is set down inside it
bumping off the leader means getting rid of whoever is first, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: panic is sudden terror
arch means slyly knowing, cunning

explanation.surface: Terrorists use wild cunning to assassinate a leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means lawless and without order, so wild in the sense of unruly.

clue.text: The Fool's lines in Lear?

parts.note: surface reading: the speeches of the Fool, the jester in Shakespeare's King Lear
setter's reading: Edward Lear, the Victorian poet of comic rhymes like The Owl and the Pussy-cat, whose foolish lines are his poems

explanation.walkthrough: King Lear's Fool speaks in riddling rhymes, but the Lear meant is Edward Lear, famous for absurd limericks.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's limericks and comic poems are the classic example of whimsical, absurd poetry: foolish lines written by Lear.

clue.text: Elite artist to depict classic heroine

parts.note: the elect are a chosen elite
RA, Royal Academician, is crossword shorthand for an artist

explanation.surface: A top painter is commissioned to portray a heroine from classical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the avenging daughter of Agamemnon in Greek tragedy, a heroine of the classics.

clue.text: Boy enthralled by libertine's embellishment

indicators.note: someone enthralled by another is held captive, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a libertine
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A young boy falls under the spell of a rake's flashy trimmings.
explanation.definitionFit: A roulade is a florid run of notes sung to one syllable, a musical embellishment.

clue.text: Book, I say, not initially the egregious example

indicators.note: not initially means without the first letter, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
'my word!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'I say!'

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims over a book that is the worst example of its kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A byword is a person or thing so notorious that its name stands for a quality, the outstanding example.

clue.text: Preliminary investigation regarding cricket club's ending of game

parts.note: re means regarding, concerning
CC is the abbreviation for cricket club

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, which is the only one kept

parts.note: the last letter of game

explanation.surface: A cricket club does some early scouting about how its match will finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting look round before acting, a preliminary investigation.

clue.text: Wit shown by one garment

parts.note: a card is a witty, eccentric person, a joker
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone shows off their humour by what they choose to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: A cardi is the British informal short form of cardigan, a knitted jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan, shortened in British speech, is a buttoned knitted top, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Decorative flooring? Keep off, preserving the peace | needed

indicators.note: preserving means keeping safe inside, so one word holds another

parts.note: to parry is to ward off a blow

indicators.note: the damaged words here seem to say a single letter is not needed, so it is dropped from the peace word

parts.note: quiet is peace

explanation.surface: A sign on a fancy floor telling people to keep off it to protect the peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The source text is damaged at the bar: the peace word must lose a single letter before going inside, so the lost words presumably said that letter was not needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquetry is flooring made of wooden blocks laid in a geometric pattern, so decorative flooring.

clue.text: Others re-evaluated really heartless feminist critique

indicators.note: something re-evaluated is reconsidered and reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a heartless word has lost its middle, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of really

explanation.surface: Other scholars have reassessed a feminist critique and found it truly lacking in feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Herstory is history told from women's point of view, a feminist challenge to male-centred accounts of the past.

clue.text: After capture, recalled nothing in brothel

parts.note: to bag is to capture, as a hunter bags game

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the following words are taken in the opposite order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, is nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is caught and afterwards remembers nothing of a night in a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After capture' puts BAG first; the reversed 'nothing in' follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagnio, from the Italian for bath, is an old word for a brothel, once used of bath-houses that served as such.

clue.text: Champion heading off competition for gallant behaviour

indicators.note: with its heading off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for champion, as in dog shows
rivalry is competition

explanation.surface: A champion who leaves the competition is praised for sporting conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champion heading' tempts a solver to take just C; Champion gives CH and it is the competition that loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry, the knightly code, now means courteous and gallant conduct, especially towards women.

clue.text: United, we had passed on, leaving one behind

parts.note: we'd is the contraction of we had

indicators.note: leaving something behind means going on without it, so a letter for one is dropped

parts.note: someone who has passed on is dead
a means one

explanation.surface: A couple, together until one died, leaving the other a widow.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedded means joined in marriage, and more widely closely joined, so united.
